policy: Merge only confirmed same-place aliases. Preserve separate facilities and existing schema; retain canonical names already referenced by rankings where possible. Existing user data is normalized at load time.

before.name: Arch of Galerius
before.overview: A monumental triumphal arch located at the junction of the Rotunda. It is one of the most famous Roman monuments in the city.
before.history_significance: Built in the early 4th century AD to commemorate Emperor Galerius's victory over the Persians. The marble panels depict the battles.
before.highlights:
The well-preserved marble panels and bas-reliefs.
 The Roman columns.
 Its position connecting the Via Regia.

before.history_significance: Built in the early 4th century AD to commemorate Emperor Galerius's victory over the Persians. The marble panels depict the battles.
before.highlights:
The well-preserved marble panels and bas-reliefs.

 Its position connecting the Via Regia.

after.name: Arch of Galerius
after.overview: A Roman triumphal arch on Egnatia Street in Thessaloniki, also known as Kamara. It is a separate monument from the nearby Rotunda.
after.history_significance: Built in the early 4th century AD to commemorate Emperor Galerius's victory over the Persians. The marble panels depict the battles.
after.highlights:
The surviving marble reliefs depicting the campaigns against the Persians.
 The three surviving piers of the original eight-pier structure.
 Its place in the Galerian palace complex.

before.name: Ben Youssef Madrasa
before.overview: An Islamic college in Marrakesh, named after the Almoravid Sultan Ali ibn Yusuf.
before.history_significance: Once the largest Islamic college in North Africa, a prime example of Marinid architecture.
before.highlights:
The elaborate stucco and mosaic decoration.
 The central courtyard with a reflecting pool.
 The student cells.

before.name: Medersa Ben Youssef
before.overview: An Islamic college in Marrakesh, one of the largest madrasas in North Africa.
before.history_significance: Refounded in the 16th century by the Saadian Sultan Abdallah al-Ghalib.
before.highlights:
The cedar wood carvings.
 The marble columns.
 The serene courtyard.

after.name: Ben Youssef Madrasa
after.overview: An Islamic college in Marrakesh, named after the Almoravid Sultan Ali ibn Yusuf.
after.history_significance: Named after the nearby Ben Youssef Mosque, the madrasa was rebuilt in the 16th century under the Saadian sultan Abdallah al-Ghalib. It became one of the major centers of Islamic learning in Morocco.
after.highlights:
The central courtyard and reflecting pool.
 Intricate zellij mosaics, carved stucco, and cedar wood decoration.
 The marble columns and former student cells.

before.name: Kilauea
before.overview: An active shield volcano in the Hawaiian Islands, and one of the most active volcanoes on Earth.
before.highlights:
Located in Hawaii Volcanoes National Park.
Features the Halemaʻumaʻu crater, legendary home of the goddess Pele.
Continuous eruptions often create new land.

before.name: Kīlauea Volcano
before.overview: An active shield volcano in the Hawaiian Islands. It is home to the Halemaʻumaʻu crater and extensive lava fields.
before.highlights:
Driving the Chain of Craters Road.
Walking through the Thurston Lava Tube.
Viewing the glow of the lava lake (when active).

after.name: Kilauea
after.overview: An active shield volcano in the Hawaiian Islands, and one of the most active volcanoes on Earth.
after.highlights:
The summit caldera and Halemaʻumaʻu crater in Hawaii Volcanoes National Park.
 The Chain of Craters Road and Thurston Lava Tube.
 Volcanic landscapes and lava viewing when conditions and park access permit.

before.name: São Paulo Museum of Art
before.overview: The most important art museum in the Southern Hemisphere, housing the largest collection of Western art in Latin America. Known by its acronym MASP.
before.history_significance: Founded in 1947 by Assis Chateaubriand and Pietro Maria Bardi. Its iconic building, designed by Lina Bo Bardi and completed in 1968, is a landmark of Brazilian modernist architecture.
before.highlights:
The glass easels displaying paintings in the main gallery.
 Works by Raphael, Rembrandt, Renoir, and Picasso.
 The iconic suspended concrete building on Paulista Avenue.

before.name: MASP (Sao Paulo Museum of Art)
before.overview: A landmark concrete and glass building suspended above the ground by two massive red beams.
before.history_significance: Designed by Lina Bo Bardi in 1968, it houses the most significant collection of Western art in the Southern Hemisphere.
before.highlights:
The crystal easel display system.
 The large open plaza beneath the suspended building.
 The panoramic view of Avenida Paulista.

after.name: São Paulo Museum of Art
after.overview: The most important art museum in the Southern Hemisphere, housing the largest collection of Western art in Latin America. Known by its acronym MASP.
after.history_significance: Founded in 1947 by Assis Chateaubriand and Pietro Maria Bardi. Its iconic building, designed by Lina Bo Bardi and completed in 1968, is a landmark of Brazilian modernist architecture.
after.highlights:
The glass easels displaying the art collection.
 The suspended building designed by Lina Bo Bardi and its open plaza.
 Works by European and Brazilian artists on Paulista Avenue.

before.name: Sao Paulo Cathedral
before.overview: A massive Neo-Gothic cathedral in the center of Sao Paulo, with a Renaissance-style dome.
before.history_significance: One of the largest Neo-Gothic temples in the world, noted for its crypt where bishops and historical figures are buried.
before.highlights:
The two 92-meter tall spires.
 The capitals carved with Brazilian flora and fauna (coffee, armadillos).
 The large pipe organ.

before.name: Sé Cathedral
before.overview: The Metropolitan Cathedral of São Paulo, a massive Neo-Gothic cathedral located at Praça da Sé in the historic center of the city.
before.history_significance: Construction began in 1913 and was fully completed only in 1954 for the city's 400th anniversary. It is one of the largest Neo-Gothic cathedrals in the world.
before.highlights:
The imposing Neo-Gothic facade with twin towers.
 The ornate interior with high vaulted ceilings.
 The crypt beneath the cathedral.

after.name: Sao Paulo Cathedral
after.overview: A massive Neo-Gothic cathedral in the center of Sao Paulo, with a Renaissance-style dome.
after.history_significance: Designed by Maximilian Hehl, the cathedral was inaugurated in 1954 for the city's 400th anniversary. Its crypt contains the tombs of bishops and historical figures, including Tibiriçá and Padre Feijó.
after.highlights:
The twin spires and Neo-Gothic facade overlooking Praça da Sé.
 The crypt containing the tombs of bishops and historical figures.
 Carved Brazilian flora and fauna and the large pipe organ.

before.name: Mercado Municipal de Sao Paulo
before.overview: A large public market housed in an eclectic-style building with stained glass windows and domes.
before.history_significance: Inaugurated in 1933, it is the gastronomic heart of Sao Paulo, famous for its vast array of fruits and foods.
before.highlights:
The famous Mortadella sandwich.
 The imported stained glass depicting farming scenes.
 The huge variety of exotic fruits.

before.name: Mercado Municipal
before.overview: São Paulo's grand municipal market, a beloved food hall housed in a magnificent early 20th-century building with stunning stained glass windows.
before.history_significance: Opened in 1933, the building was designed by Ramos de Azevedo. The colorful stained glass windows depicting farm life are among the most recognized images of São Paulo.
before.highlights:
The enormous stained glass windows.
 The famous mortadella sandwich (mortadela).
 The vast array of fresh produce, spices, and Brazilian foods.

after.name: Mercado Municipal de Sao Paulo
after.overview: A large public market housed in an eclectic-style building with stained glass windows and domes.
after.history_significance: Opened in 1933, the building was designed by Ramos de Azevedo. The colorful stained glass windows depicting farm life are among the most recognized images of São Paulo.
after.highlights:
The famous Mortadella sandwich.
 The imported stained glass depicting farming scenes.
 The huge variety of exotic fruits.

before.name: Shilin Stone Forest
before.overview: A notable set of limestone formations located in Yunnan Province. The tall rocks resemble petrified trees creating a forest of stone.
before.highlights:
Walking through the maze of towering stone pinnacles.
Visiting the Ashima Rock associated with local legend.
Experiencing the unique karst geography.

before.name: Stone Forest
before.overview: A spectacular UNESCO World Heritage geological park featuring massive, towering limestone formations that genuinely resemble a petrified forest.
before.highlights:
Navigating the maze-like paths through the towering, razor-sharp karst pillars
 Spotting the famous 'Ashima' stone, tied to a poignant local Sani legend
 Photographing the surreal, otherworldly landscape from the elevated viewing pavilions

after.name: Shilin Stone Forest
after.overview: A notable set of limestone formations located in Yunnan Province. The tall rocks resemble petrified trees creating a forest of stone.
after.highlights:
Walking through the maze of towering stone pinnacles.
Visiting the Ashima Rock associated with local legend.
Experiencing the unique karst geography.

after.name: Park Alisa

after.highlights:
Its historic site in Alexandrovsky Park.
 Family rides and a Caterpillar roller coaster documented in amusement-park records.

after.name: Park Yulya
after.overview: An amusement park established by Vostok on Prospekt Prosveshcheniya in northern Saint Petersburg.
after.highlights:
Its historic site at 80 Prospekt Prosveshcheniya.
 Imported amusement rides and family entertainment.
after.history_significance: Founded in 2000 as Vostok's first amusement park, before the company developed the separate Alisa park.

distinct_places.coordinate_note: Alisa uses a published park coordinate rounded to four decimals. Yulya is an approximate historical-address marker for 80 Prospekt Prosveshcheniya, not a surveyed entrance. Current operation is not asserted.
